ranked.label: MACULA exact Hebrew morph surfaces with Cherith English definitions

shapes.test: '~' with one space on each side and a word on each side
shapes.means: A gap inside one English phrase: the place where English that belongs to another Hebrew word or morph of the verse stands ('bring ~ back' reads 'bring [him] back'; 'corner of ~ garment' reads 'corner of [his] garment'). It is notation inside one reading.

shapes.test: '~' at the first character of the route, glued to the word after it
shapes.means: The same gap, standing before this word's English: English carried by another word comes first ('~south', '~rise of').

shapes.test: '~' at the last character of the route, glued to the word before it
shapes.means: The same gap, standing after this word's English ('apart~').

shapes.test: '’' between 'n' and 't' (n’t)
shapes.means: The apostrophe of a contracted negative ('don’t'); a letter-level mark inside one word.

shapes.test: '’' after a letter and before a final 's' or 'S' that ends the word
shapes.means: The possessive ’s on one word ('donkey’s', 'Merari’s', 'LORD’S'); part of the word.

shapes.test: '’' after a word-final 's' with no letter after it
shapes.means: The plural possessive s’ ('eagles’', 'sons’'); part of the word.

shapes.test: '-' with a letter immediately on each side
shapes.means: Joins two parts into one word or one name ('father-in-law', 'one-fifth', 'beth-arabah', 'Esh-baal'); notation inside one reading.

shapes.test: '-' at the first character of the route, glued to the word after it
shapes.means: The English is a bound suffix that attaches to the English of a neighboring word ('-self'); one reading, written as a suffix.

shapes.test: '!' as the last character of the route, directly after a letter
shapes.means: The gloss's own mood: an imperative or exclamation ('count!', 'far be it!'); part of the one reading.

shapes.test: '!' as the last character of the route, after a space
shapes.means: The same mood mark, set off by a space ('love !'); part of the one reading.

shapes.test: '?' as the last character of the route, directly after a letter
shapes.means: The gloss is interrogative ('how?', 'how many?'); part of the one reading.

shapes.test: '?' as the last character of the route, after a space
shapes.means: The same interrogative mark, set off by a space ('for why ?'); part of the one reading.

shapes.test: '(' of a parenthesis holding only a number (digits, then at most one letter)
shapes.means: A lexicon number tying this name-part to the compound name it belongs to: the two halves of one name carry the same number ('Ben (1128)' with 'Deker (1128)'; 'Ben (1127)' with 'Geber (1127)'). An annotation, not a reading.

shapes.test: '(' of a parenthesis holding only number=number+number (each number digits, then at most one letter)
shapes.means: A cross-reference in the provider's lexicon numbering, standing where an English gloss would: the entry on the left is composed of the entries on the right. No English at all.

shapes.test: '(' of a parenthesis of English words that encloses the whole route
shapes.means: The whole English is marked as supplied: an implied word rather than a rendering of letters this form carries ('(namely)' on a conjunction). One reading.

shapes.test: '(' of a parenthesis of English words standing beside other words of the route
shapes.means: One word of the gloss is marked as supplied for sense ('face of (him)', '(just) above'); notation inside one reading.

shapes.test: ')' of a parenthesis holding only a number (digits, then at most one letter)
shapes.means: A lexicon number tying this name-part to the compound name it belongs to: the two halves of one name carry the same number ('Ben (1128)' with 'Deker (1128)'; 'Ben (1127)' with 'Geber (1127)'). An annotation, not a reading.

shapes.test: ')' of a parenthesis holding only number=number+number (each number digits, then at most one letter)
shapes.means: A cross-reference in the provider's lexicon numbering, standing where an English gloss would: the entry on the left is composed of the entries on the right. No English at all.

shapes.test: ')' of a parenthesis of English words that encloses the whole route
shapes.means: The whole English is marked as supplied: an implied word rather than a rendering of letters this form carries ('(namely)' on a conjunction). One reading.

shapes.test: ')' of a parenthesis of English words standing beside other words of the route
shapes.means: One word of the gloss is marked as supplied for sense ('face of (him)', '(just) above'); notation inside one reading.

shapes.test: '=' inside a parenthesis whose content is number=number+number
shapes.means: Is composed of: the left entry number equals the sum on the right.

shapes.test: '+' inside a parenthesis whose content is number=number+number
shapes.means: And: joins the component entry numbers. Not Strong's KJV '+' (supplied word) — this provider never uses '+' outside these equations.

shapes.test: '.' at the first character of the route, glued to the word after it
shapes.means: A full stop with nothing before it in the field, glued to 'and'. It ends nothing this route holds, so it divides nothing; the data has one instance and cannot say whether it is a stray or the end of the preceding English sentence carried onto this conjunction.

shapes.test: '/' with a letter immediately on each side
shapes.means: Alternation between two renderings of one head that share the words after them: 'thumbs/big toes of' is 'thumbs of' or 'big toes of'. A reader sees two readings, but the shared tail belongs to both, so a cut at the slash leaves the first without its 'of'.

readings.ship_whole: one reading, 'thumbs/big toes of', as today (1 route, 1 piece)
readings.separate_at_slash: two pieces, 'thumbs' and 'big toes of' (1 route, 2 pieces); the first prints without the 'of' both share

readings.a_reading: print the equation as this provider's reading for the article, as today (2 routes, no English in them)
readings.an_annotation: treat a route of numbers alone as an annotation with no English reading, so this provider puts no pill there (2 routes)

readings.part_of_reading: the lexicon number prints inside the reading as written, as today (4 routes)
readings.set_apart: the page shows the number as the provider's cross-reference beside the name-part, not as words of the reading (4 routes; the characters stay, only their presentation differs)

readings.stray: a stray full stop, printed as written (1 route)
readings.carried_sentence_end: the end of the preceding English sentence carried onto the conjunction (1 route); either way nothing divides

v3_comparison.engine: gloss-store packSplit at depth-0 ';', then sense-split-rule-v3-a-comma-divides-glosses-never-a-sentence on each sense; a damaged sense prints nothing
